title: Unawareness of privacy implications during registration
description: Homeowner shares personal account details and device information without full awareness of how this data will be used, stored, or shared by the Home Hub.
uncertainty_note: Node ID is a best guess without reference material

title: Excessive disclosure of personal data on receipt
description: Home Hub processes and stores identifiable information from account registration and sensor enrollment, leading to potential privacy disclosure if not minimized.
uncertainty_note: Node ID approximate based on typical LINDDUN Pro trees for data receipt

title: Linkability through registration metadata
description: Data flow metadata during registration could link the homeowner's identity to specific home devices and locations.
uncertainty_note: Node ID uncertain without exact threat tree reference

title: Guest unawareness of logging
description: The guest enters the temporary access code without realizing the Home Hub may log the entry event, associating it with their visit and potentially tracking movements or access patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate without reference material; this fits unawareness of processing at data subject/source.

title: Disclosure via access log
description: Home Hub processes and potentially stores the temporary code usage, disclosing the guest's access details to system administrators or through breaches.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; based on disclosure of information during processing at destination.

title: Linkability of access event
description: The data flow of the access code could enable linking the guest's identity or timing to the specific door unlock action if metadata or code is traceable.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; data-centric linkability threat on the flow.

title: Linkability of events to individuals via log storage
description: Storing motion/door/sensor events in the local event log enables linking multiple events over time to infer presence, routines or identities of household members.
assumptions: Log is queryable or exportable by the hub or other processes
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on typical LINDDUN Pro linkability trees for data storage

title: Disclosure of sensitive home activity data
description: The event log at DS1 may disclose detailed information about private home activities (e.g., when residents are home or moving between rooms) if accessed by unauthorized parties or through side-channel attacks.
assumptions: Physical or logical access to the datastore could occur

title: Unawareness of data logging by home hub
description: Residents may be unaware that the Home Hub (P1) is persistently logging sensor events to the local datastore, preventing informed consent or control over their data.
assumptions: No explicit user notification or dashboard for log contents

title: Unawareness of clip upload
description: Homeowners may be unaware that recorded clips containing personal activities are being shared with cloud storage by the Home Hub process.
assumptions: Users have not been explicitly informed of all upload destinations and retention
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on typical LINDDUN Pro U tree structure for unawareness of processing

title: Disclosure of video content at rest
description: Cloud Video Storage may expose or leak identifiable video clips to unauthorized internal staff or external parties due to insufficient access controls or breaches.
assumptions: Storage provider employees or attackers can access raw clips
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; typical for disclosure threats in data stores

title: Linkability through upload metadata
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timing, volume, endpoints) can be used to link specific home activities or identities to the cloud account.
assumptions: Adversary can observe network traffic to/from the Home Hub
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate for flow-based linkability threats

title: Linkability of motion alerts via metadata
description: Real-time motion alert timing and frequency metadata in transit can link specific home activities or presence to identifiable users or households.

title: Disclosure of occupancy and activity data
description: Mobile App Backend receives and processes/stores the motion alert revealing personal home occupancy and movement patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best estimate without reference material

title: Detectability of motion events by transmission
description: Act of Home Hub sending the alert makes motion detection events detectable to the receiving backend and any intermediaries.

title: Disclosure of sensitive home activity via notification interception
description: Motion detection notifications pushed over the flow may contain details about home events; if not end-to-end encrypted, intermediaries or attackers could intercept and learn about occupancy or security incidents.
assumptions: Push notifications use standard mobile push services which may have access to payload metadata or content.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate as exact LINDDUN Pro tree for notification flows not recalled precisely; focuses on data disclosure in transit.

title: Disclosure of motion events on recipient device
description: Notifications appearing on the homeowner's phone (e.g., lock screen) could be viewed by unauthorized persons nearby, revealing that motion was detected and potentially indicating whether the home is occupied or under surveillance.
assumptions: Notifications display event details without requiring device unlock or app authentication.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate based on typical disclosure threats at data recipient/storage; may also relate to unawareness if user not informed of visibility risks.

title: Linkability of homeowner to specific motion events by backend
description: By sending targeted notifications, the backend links the homeowner's identity/device with precise timing and details of detected motions, enabling profiling of daily routines or presence patterns.
assumptions: Backend maintains user accounts and correlates notifications with user profiles.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; this is a data-centric linkability threat originating from the sharer's decision to send identifiable event data.

title: User unawareness of aggregated analytics sharing
description: Mobile app backend shares device-usage analytics with third-party vendor without ensuring end-users are aware of or have consented to this specific sharing, even if aggregated.
assumptions: Users of the mobile app are the data subjects whose usage is being aggregated.

title: Disclosure through insufficient aggregation
description: Cloud analytics vendor receives aggregated data that may still allow inference or partial disclosure of individual device usage patterns if aggregation parameters are weak.
uncertainty_note: Depends on exact aggregation method and data granularity, which is not specified.

title: Linkability via communication metadata
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timing, volume, endpoints) between P2 and EE3 could be used to link the mobile app's backend activity to the specific analytics vendor.

title: Disclosure of sensitive video content from storage
description: The Cloud Video Storage shares personal video clips (potentially showing homeowners, family members, or home interiors) with the backend upon retrieval request, risking unauthorized disclosure if access controls are insufficient.
assumptions: Retrieval is authenticated but storage may lack end-to-end encryption or fine-grained access logging.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on typical LINDDUN Pro disclosure trees; no reference material used.

title: Linkability through retrieval metadata
description: Data flow metadata (e.g., video clip size, retrieval timing, or frequency) from DS2 to P2 can be used to link specific video access events back to an individual homeowner's activity patterns.
assumptions: Adversary can observe network traffic or logs of the flow.
uncertainty_note: Node id chosen as best fit for linkability in data flows; uncertain without exact tree reference.

title: Detectability of video playback activity
description: The Mobile App Backend's receipt and processing of the video clip makes the homeowner's surveillance or monitoring activity detectable, potentially revealing presence or security status at home.
assumptions: Backend processes or logs the retrieval in a way observable by insiders or compromised systems.
